'''Amondawa''' is one of the 8 living varieties of the [[Kagwahiva language]], a [[Tupi–Guarani language]] of the state of [[Rondônia]] in Brazil.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.2 - Amundava |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/amun1246 |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref> It is spoken by 81 of the Amondawa people, who numbered 130 in 2017. There are also 10 [[Passive speaker (language)|passive bilingual]] speakers who can only understand the language but not speak it. Amondawa children are no longer learning the language, resulting in its endangerment and possible future extinction.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |last=Nascimento dos Santos |first=Wesley |title=Topics on the syntax of Kawahíva: A Tupí-Guaraní language from the Brazilian Amazon |date=2024 |publisher=UC Berkeley |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/1h26s7sq |language=en}}</ref> Other sources report that Amondawa is being taught in schools in the region, however.<ref>{{Citation |title=Mixing and Mapping: Motion, Path, and Manner in Amondawa |date=2010-10-18 |work=Crosslinguistic Approaches to the Psychology of Language |pages=447–460 |editor-last=Guo |editor-first=Jiansheng |url=https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/artigo%3Asampaio-2009/Sinha_et_al_2009_Mixing_and_Mapping.pdf |access-date=2025-09-12 |edition=0 |publisher=Psychology Press |language=en |doi=10.4324/9780203837887-47 |isbn=978-0-203-83788-7 |editor2-last=Lieven |editor2-first=Elena |editor3-last=Budwig |editor3-first=Nancy |editor4-last=Ervin-Tripp |editor4-first=Susan}}</ref> The Amondawa language lacks numerals above four and its speakers do not have an abstract sense of time,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Telling Time in Amondawa - The Rosetta Project |url=https://rosettaproject.org/blog/02011/may/27/telling-time-in-amondawa/ |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=rosettaproject.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-05-20 |title=Amondawa tribe lacks abstract idea of time, study says |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-13452711 |access-date=2025-09-12 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sinha |first=Chris |last2=Sinha |first2=Vera Da Silva |last3=Zinken |first3=Jörg |last4=Sampaio |first4=Wany |date=March 2011 |title=When time is not space: The social and linguistic construction of time intervals and temporal event relations in an Amazonian culture |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/langcog.2011.006/html |journal=Language and Cognition |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=137–169 |doi=10.1515/langcog.2011.006 |issn=1866-9808}}</ref> leading to media outlets reporting the Amondawa as "the tribe without time".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinha |first=Chris |title=About time: The tribe without time |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg21128331-000-about-time-the-tribe-without-time/ |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref>
